subject: Exhibit B pricing stabilizer: trigger definition & proposed redline
messages:
From: Andrew Huang <andrew.huang@brightwave.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@brightwave.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit B pricing stabilizer — clarification on trigger and relief

Laura / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the Order Form and flagged the Exhibit B 'stabilizer' language (section 3.2: Stabilization Trigger). We need a sharper definition of the trigger and an operational relief path — specifically: when Brightwave spikes above forecast for two consecutive months, how is the cap/floor applied, who calculates it, and can Brightwave appeal the calculation?

High level asks:
- Clarify the trigger (consecutive months? rolling 30-day?)
- Define who provides notice and the timeframe to cure/appeal (Brightwave needs 10 business days)
- Make the fee cap apply to billed tokens in the month the trigger is identified, not retroactively beyond 30 days

We attached our suggested redline of Exhibit B (Brightwave_Redline_ExhibitB_v1.pdf). Please let us know if Redwood has a standard counter-language — we're trying to avoid multiple back-and-forths with legal.

Andrew
Purchasing Manager | Brightwave Systems
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Andrew Huang <andrew.huang@brightwave.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, contracts@brightwave.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit B pricing stabilizer — clarification on trigger and relief

Andrew — thanks for the clear bullets and the redline. I copied Marissa (account lead) so we have alignment on commercial tradeoffs. High level response and next steps below, then I'll loop legal for line edits.

Short answers:
- Trigger: we support a 'two consecutive calendar months' standard (we typically measure calendar months to keep billing cleanup simple).
- Calculation & notice: Redwood will run the initial calculation and provide a written notice with the month-over-month delta and supporting metrics. Brightwave gets a 10 business day period to contest with alternative telemetry.
- Retroactivity: agree on limiting adjustments to the 30-day window prior to notice; we can accept no retroactive billing beyond that window.

We have a commercial ask: if the stabilizer is triggered repeatedly (more than 3 triggers in a rolling 12 months), we need a path to request add'l capacity or a temporary surcharge to preserve predictability for our capacity planning. We propose an explicit 'escalation credit' option.

I'll attach a Redwood-proposed markup for Exhibit B and ask Karthik (legal) to verify phrasing for notice, cure and the three-trigger escalator. Expect a follow-up today.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_ExhibitB_v2.pdf (markup)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exhibit B pricing stabilizer — need quick legal redline

Karthik — forwarding Brightwave's redline and our proposed商业 note above. TL;DR: we agreed to two consecutive calendar months, 10 business day contest window, and limit retroactivity to 30 days prior to notice. Commercial wants a 3-trigger escalator/credit path.

Can you:
1) Confirm the notice/cure wording is legally safe (avoid open-ended audit obligations);
2) Draft concrete language for: measurement authority, contest process, and 3-trigger escalator mechanics (we'll offer either a one-time capacity credit or temporary surcharge by mutual agreement);
3) Keep it consumer-friendly — Brightwave is sensitive to retroactive charges.

Deadline: EOD today if possible — they want to get this into their contract round this week.

Thanks,
Laura
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exhibit B pricing stabilizer — quick legal redline

Laura / Marissa,

Thanks for the context. I made line edits in the attached markup and drafted a compact definition set below to include in Exhibit B. Key moves:
- Use 'measurement period' = calendar month; 'stabilization trigger' = "exceeded forecast by >=20% for two consecutive calendar months" (numeric threshold reduces ambiguity).
- Calculation & notice: Redwood to provide a detailed Notice of Stabilization with token counts, API route breakdown, and gross/monthly totals. Brightwave has 10 business days from receipt to provide a written dispute and supporting telemetry. If disputed, parties will exchange evidence; if unresolved in 20 business days, an independent third-party measurement (mutually agreed vendor) will make a binding determination (costs split 50/50).
- Retroactivity: adjustments limited to invoices issued in the 30-day lookback before Notice date; no other retrospective billing.
- Escalator: after three stabilization triggers in a rolling 12-month window, Brightwave may elect (i) a one-time 15% capacity credit applied to the next billing month, or (ii) negotiate a temporary surcharge up to 10% (defined by a simple calculator) to preserve provisioning. Either option must be mutually agreed in good faith within 30 days of the third trigger notice.

Redwood's redline file: Brightwave_Redline_ExhibitB_v3.pdf attached. I've kept the language operational and constrained liability. If you want, I can prepare a short summary paragraph for Andrew to make the commercial tradeoff explicit.

Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Karthik_ExhibitB_LineEdits.pdf
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit B pricing stabilizer — clarification on trigger and relief

Andrew — attaching Redwood's clean and marked Exhibit B (Brightwave_Redline_ExhibitB_v3.pdf) that implements the items below:
- Stabilization trigger: >=20% over forecast for two consecutive calendar months.
- Notice & contest: Redwood issues Notice with supporting metrics; Brightwave has 10 business days to dispute; unresolved disputes escalate to an independent measurement (costs split).
- Retroactivity limited to 30 days prior to Notice.
- Escalator: after 3 triggers in rolling 12 months, Brightwave may choose either a one-time 15% capacity credit for the next month or negotiate a temporary surcharge (up to 10%) — both require mutual good-faith agreement within 30 days.

Commercial note: We included the escalator to preserve capacity predictability for both sides. If Brightwave prefers an explicit capacity ramp (milestone-based committed capacity) instead of the escalator, we can model that in the Order Schedule — happy to run numbers with Marissa.

Next step: please review the attached markup and confirm whether the threshold and remedy choices are acceptable. If you accept, we can incorporate these changes into the orderform and route for signature.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
